paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: nobody out-arrogants the LORD. Babylon was "the hammer of the whole earth," and she still got caught in a snare "before you knew it," because she "challenged the LORD" (Jeremiah 50:23-24). I have stood on a bakery floor feeling like the biggest stamper in the kitchen, and then a rolling pin said hello. Pride is a lot of noise, and it falls over fast.

Now look at who God is standing beside. Israel and Judah were oppressed, and their captors were "refusing to release them," and I think that was a heavy place to be (Jeremiah 50:33). But "Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is His name," and He "will fervently plead their case" (Jeremiah 50:34). God sees people who are held fast, and He doesn't lose to whoever is holding them.

So what do you do with this today, friend? Trust the Redeemer more than you trust whatever looks big and loud right now. God asks, "For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me?" (Jeremiah 50:44). Nobody, and that's good news for everyone who belongs to Him. The story isn't over, so keep your apron on.
